summary: Implemented the device detail screen, replacing WU004's placeholder: general information, system metrics, a Docker container table with distinct offline/Docker-unavailable/empty states, registered services, and a session-scoped recent-activity feed sourced from the live notification://ready event stream. Frontend-only; 152 backend tests unaffected.
completed: features/devices/DeviceDetailScreen.tsx: header with back button, status dot/chip, Open Terminal (disabled -- WU016 scope), Refresh, and a settings-gear button; two-column General Information + System Metrics / Recent Activity layout matching the design's 1.3fr/1fr grid; full-width Docker container table with three distinct empty states (device offline, Docker unavailable while device stays online, zero containers); services grid with an explicit empty state.
Reused WU013's useDeviceSnapshots hook (single-id array) so the screen updates live via the existing device://snapshot-updated event, no new backend surface needed.

stores/useDeviceActivity.ts: session-scoped recent-activity feed subscribing to notification://ready, filtered per device, capped at 20 entries. Documented and enforced (via key={deviceId} in AppShell.tsx) that switching devices remounts the screen rather than the hook self-resetting, since a synchronous reset inside the effect body correctly tripped the react-hooks/set-state-in-effect rule.
lib/formatting/containerStatus.ts: label/color-class helpers for DockerContainerState and DockerHealthStatus, plus formatPorts().
types/notification.ts: TypeScript mirror of the Rust NotificationEvent struct (WU012).
Verified npm run build and npm run lint (0 errors, same 3 pre-existing warnings) pass; cargo test still 152/152.

validationCommands.summary: 0 errors, 3 pre-existing HMR-granularity warnings (unrelated to this WU).
152/152 unit tests passed, unaffected (no backend changes this WU).

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: Device detail view reflects the latest snapshot for the selected device
acceptanceCriteria.evidence: DeviceDetailScreen derives all metrics/containers/status directly from useDeviceSnapshots(deviceId), the same live hook and backend event used by WU013's dashboard; live smoke test confirmed the offline snapshot shape written to state.json is exactly what the screen's offline branches render.

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: A Docker permission or unavailability error shows a clear message without hiding valid system metrics
acceptanceCriteria.evidence: The Docker Containers section checks snapshot.dockerAvailable independently of the System Metrics panel above it -- an online device with dockerAvailable=false shows its own 'Docker is not available' message (including any warnings) in that section only, while CPU/MEM/DISK/TEMP continue to render normally.

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: Navigating back returns to the dashboard preserving its state
acceptanceCriteria.evidence: Back button calls the existing goDashboard() router action; DashboardScreen re-fetches its own device list on mount (unchanged from WU013), and the router's screen stack was not modified in a way that could lose dashboard-level UI state.

notes: Risk score: 10/100 (low). Rationale: purely additive frontend work consuming already-tested backend commands/events; no new backend surface, no persistence changes.

Recent Activity is intentionally session-scoped, not backed by persisted history -- the backend (WU012) only emits notification://ready live and does not currently write a transition-history log to disk. This is a deliberate scope decision to stay within this WU's frontend-only suggested files rather than adding new backend persistence; a persisted activity log could be a future work unit if the user wants activity to survive an app restart.

Terminal button remains disabled pending WU016 (open_device_terminal). Clicking a registered service navigates to the Services screen filtered to this device (goServices(deviceId)) rather than opening the browser directly, since open_device_service is also WU016 scope.

Could not capture a visual screenshot this session for the same reason as WU013 (active fullscreen use of the desktop); verified via a clean TypeScript build and a live smoke test against real backend-emitted snapshot data instead.
